analysis.investment_thesis: Capri Global Capital is a genuinely exciting MSME and home loan NBFC with a 37.2% revenue CAGR and 30.4% profit CAGR over nine years — the kind of compounding machine that would have been a classic SMILE pick at INR 500–1,500 Cr market cap. At INR 17,524 Cr today the discovery has happened, but the growth runway in underpenetrated MSME credit remains substantial if execution holds.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 37.2% and profit CAGR of 30.4% over 9 years is exceptional compounding — FY25 PAT of INR 479 Cr is nearly 11x the FY16 PAT of INR 44 Cr
Promoter at 59.92% with strong conviction; strong recent equity raise (equity jumped from INR 3,837 Cr to INR 6,673 Cr in FY25) signals growth confidence
Operates in MSME lending and affordable home loans — both massively underpenetrated markets aligned with India's formalization megatrend; Forward P/E of 12.96x is reasonable for this growth rate
key_risks: D/E of 2.52 is high even for an NBFC; total debt at INR 15,577 Cr growing 3x in 3 years — in a credit cycle downturn, NPAs can rapidly erode the thin equity cushion
Finance costs compounding at 67.9% CAGR (INR 12 Cr in FY16 to INR 1,274 Cr in FY25) — cost of funds pressure in a rising rate environment could squeeze NIMs sharply

OCF negative every single year for the last 5 years (total outflow ~INR 13,000 Cr) as loan book expands — the business entirely depends on continuous external capital raise; any market disruption halts growth
red_flags: Market cap INR 17,524 Cr — 17x outside my sweet spot; institutional investors (DII 20%) have already discovered and bid up the stock
OCF 0/5 positive years — while normal for a lending NBFC, the scale of cash burn (INR 4,312 Cr outflow in FY25) creates existential refinancing dependency
P/S of 7.2x for an NBFC — if NPA cycle hits and growth slows, this multiple compresses violently
analysis.detailed_analysis:
If I imagine turning back the clock to 2018–2019 when Capri Global had a market cap of INR 1,000–2,000 Cr and was growing at 30%+ in MSME lending — that was the entry point I dream about. The business has all the SMILE DNA: underpenetrated market (MSME formal credit is <10% of TAM), promoter with skin in the game, management building a serious institution, and secular India formalization tailwind. The nine-year compounding record is one of the better ones I see in this batch.

Today the opportunity is priced. At INR 17,524 Cr market cap and P/E 20.8x, much of the growth is in the price. More importantly, the D/E of 2.52 and the explosive growth in finance costs (INR 1,274 Cr in FY25) mean any credit quality deterioration or liquidity squeeze — like we saw with IL&FS and DHFL — can rapidly turn this into a value destroyer. I would watch the quarterly NPA numbers and credit costs very carefully. If the stock corrects 30–40% to bring it closer to P/E 12–14x and if asset quality remains clean, this moves into BUY territory for me.
